description: Source for the Gemini extension policies, rendered by scripts/build-gemini-hooks.sh (CI runs its --check): `rules` -> policies/tamirs-superpowers.toml, `permission_rules` -> policies/tamirs-superpowers-permissions.toml. Gemini CLI loads every policies/*.toml at an extension's root as tier-2 rules and honours only deny/ask_user there: 'Gemini CLI ignores any allow decisions or yolo mode configurations in extension policies' (extension reference; loadExtensionPolicies drops both). So these files state STATICALLY - a regex over the shell command (commandRegex), over the JSON-stringified tool arguments (argsPattern), or an MCP tool name (mcpName + toolName) - what must hold even when hooks are disabled with /hooks disable-all or fail open (Gemini has no onFailure). `rules` mirror the guards this plugin already runs and are all deny. `permission_rules` are ADR 004 D8's static layer: ask_user for R4 command forms (mode-less, so they hold under --yolo and deny with no TTY, measured G3) and deny for what the ADR denies outright. The generator refuses allow, modes, an ask_user on anything but R4, and an ask_user priority that is not below the deny priority. A user-tier rule (~/.gemini/policies) or an "Always allow" outranks every rule here; that is the user's own route, written outside the agent session (the agent may not write it, ADR 004 D10.1).
regex_macros_note: Gemini matches commandRegex as `"command":"<regex>` over the stable-stringified arguments, so a regex is anchored at the start of the command; a compound command is split and every part is checked on its own. Gemini also DROPS, with only a warning, any pattern its isSafeRegExp calls a nested quantifier (a group holding a quantifier, then any `)` followed by * + ? or {), so no pattern here has a quantifier after a closing parenthesis: an optional group is written `(?:x|)` and a repeat is spelled out. ENV = up to three leading VAR=value assignments, GIT = git and up to two global options, BIN = an optional directory before a program, SH = an optional interpreter and path before a script, END = the end of a word (whitespace, the closing quote of the stringified command, or the end).

rules.mirrors: core/policies/git.md: 'No force-push to base_branch or to a branch another task is working on'. Static form: no force-push anywhere; --force-with-lease is deliberately NOT matched (the next character after --force is '-', not whitespace, the closing quote of the stringified command, or end), because a lease push is how pr-dev rebases its own branch.
rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers policy: `git push --force`/`-f` is denied. core/policies/git.md forbids force-pushing the base branch or a branch another task holds; use --force-with-lease on a branch you own, or ask the user.

rules.mirrors: core/policies/git.md: a branch with unmerged work is live work and is not deleted. `git branch -D` (and -rD/-Dr, `--delete --force`) discards unmerged commits without a merge check; plain `-d` refuses, which is the point.
rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers policy: `git branch -D` is denied — it discards unmerged work without a merge check. Use `git branch -d` (refuses when unmerged) or ask the user.

rules.mirrors: hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh lockfile rule: *.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb, go.sum are generated by a package manager, never hand-edited.
rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers policy: that path is a package-manager lockfile — it is generated, never hand-edited. Change the manifest (package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml / go.mod) and re-run the package manager.

rules.mirrors: hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh .yarn/releases/ rule: the vendored Yarn binary.
rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers policy: .yarn/releases/ holds the vendored Yarn binary. Change it with `yarn set version <version>`, not by editing the file.

rules.mirrors: hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh .github/workflows/ rule: a workflow change is R4 workflow.edit (ADR 004 D1, D10.5); the user approves and makes it, never a route around the guard.
rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers policy: .github/workflows/ files are not edited by the agent. Changing a workflow is an R4 action (workflow.edit): ask the user to approve this exact change and to make it themselves, rather than routing it through another tool or a remote API.

not_expressible: A push to a branch another agent currently holds (hooks/protect-other-branches.sh): the answer depends on live claim files under the shared claim directory, not on the command text.
Worktree isolation (hooks/enforce-worktree-edits.sh): whether a path is the main checkout or a registered worktree is git state, not a path shape.
Build output under dist/, build/, out/ (guard-sensitive-files.sh): denied only when git ignores the path, which a static pattern cannot ask.
shadcn components/ui/ (guard-sensitive-files.sh): denied only when components.json exists in the repo.
Writes made THROUGH a shell command (`cat > yarn.lock`, `sed -i`, `tee`): argsPattern sees only the tool's own arguments; the hook's write-target parser covers that shape.
Durable Docker state (hooks/docker-guard.py): a judgement over run arguments, not a literal to match.

An override for an intended edit: the hook's PM_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1 unlocks its generated-file rules only, and an extension policy has no environment switch at all. The user's own route is a user-tier rule in ~/.gemini/policies/, written outside the agent session.

permission_rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers permission policy: `--no-verify` skips the repository's hooks (git.verify.skip, core/policies/safety.md invariant 6). It is an R4 action (ADR 004), never automatic at any level: it needs your approval at a host prompt, so with no one at the terminal it is denied.

Do not retry it through another tool, command or path.

permission_rules.mirrors: ADR 004 D8 GitHub MCP server flags: excluded at every level. pr.merge is R3 and never automatic; the repository tools are R4.
permission_rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers permission policy: this GitHub MCP tool is excluded at every level (ADR 004 D8). The only automatic merge is `gh pr merge --auto`, and repository creation and deletion ask on the gh path.

permission_rules.mirrors: ADR 004 D8 GitHub MCP server flags: tools whose arguments can reach R3/R4 stay excluded until the platform's MCP hook matcher is verified live. On Gemini permission-guard.sh is wired to this server's tools (BeforeTool on mcp_github_<tool>, which gemini-wrap.sh maps to the Claude tool names), but that it fires for an extension server's tools is source-read (0.60.0), not measured, and hooks can be disabled; this static deny holds either way. r is the highest level the arguments can reach.
permission_rules.denyMessage: tamirs-superpowers permission policy: on Gemini this GitHub MCP tool is excluded at every level (ADR 004 D8): its arguments can reach R3/R4, and the permission guard's hook on this server's tools is not yet verified live, so this static rule decides. The same change through the gh CLI is checked by the permission guard.

permission_not_expressible: fs.delete.tree (a recursive rm of /, a top-level directory, the home directory or a direct child, or a git repository root): it judges the resolved path, which a static prefix rule cannot; permission-guard.sh decides it on BeforeTool run_shell_command.

Level-dependent decisions (R2 and R3: ask at supervised, allow at standard or unattended): a static rule cannot read the level, so hooks/permission-guard.sh decides them and answers deny with the setting that would allow it.

R4 forms that depend on state: worktree.remove.force, worktree.drop and git.reset_to_remote only when they discard uncommitted or unpushed work; git.push.force.default to a default branch other than main or master.

The REST and GraphQL equivalents of the R4 actions beyond the named protection, ruleset and release forms (gh api with a variable path, curl to api.github.com, file-sourced GraphQL): permission-guard.sh maps or treats them as UNCLASSIFIED (R4).
Wrappers and interpreters (make, eval, xargs, a script this catalog does not name, python3 -c, node -e): seen by no layer (ADR 004 Open risks).

Protected paths that depend on the repository root or the plugin root ({repo}/.gemini/settings.json, {repo}/.gemini/policies/**, {repo}/opencode.json, {repo}/.opencode/plugin/**, {plugin_root}/hooks/**): guard-sensitive-files.sh resolves both; writes made through a shell command likewise.

The GitHub MCP tools of R2 (create_pull_request, add_issue_comment, ...): level-dependent, so no static rule can decide them. hooks/permission-guard.sh does, on BeforeTool mcp_github_<tool>: gemini-wrap.sh maps the bundled server's calls to the Claude tool names (from mcp_context when it names server github, else by the mcp_github_ prefix) and delivers any ask as a deny (G1); the server flags stand behind it.
